profile.research_note:
Building identity as a facility distinct from Union Pacific Center headquarters not independently confirmed. Revisit with fresh WebSearch budget.

[batch narration moved out of reading 2026-09-02] This facility in Omaha, Nebraska is named for Jack Koraleski, a longtime Union Pacific executive who served as vice chairman and later chief executive officer before his 2015 retirement and was inducted into the University of Nebraska Omaha business hall of fame. Union Pacific Railroad, together with its parent Union Pacific Corporation, is a Class I freight railroad headquartered at Union Pacific Center, a 317 foot office tower at 1400 Douglas Street in downtown Omaha that opened in June 2004. Union Pacific and other large railroads commonly name major facilities after former senior executives. This research confirmed Koraleski role at Union Pacific and the company Omaha headquarters through the company own investor and news materials and University of Nebraska Omaha alumni profiles, but did not find a published, dedicated source describing a Jack Koraleski Technology, Research and Development Center as a distinct building separate from Union Pacific Center, nor any capacity or infrastructure specification for it. As a large, technology intensive freight railroad, Union Pacific is known to operate significant internal IT infrastructure supporting train dispatching, logistics, and safety systems, consistent with an enterprise private data center, but that is an inference rather than a confirmed published fact. This research was carried out at the operator level in an earlier phase of this project.
